property_summary: For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for IAccessControl and IERC165 interface IDs and false only for unrelated IDs; the buggy version breaks this by always returning false.

For any interfaceId, the reference supportsInterface returns true for the IAccessControl interfaceId (since AccessControl also supports IERC165 via super), while the buggy version always returns false.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for at least the IERC165 interface ID; the buggy version always returns false, violating this rule.
For any interfaceId, the reference supportsInterface returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID (type(IAccessControl).interfaceId), while the buggy version returns false.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return the same result as calling supportsInterface on the contract itself; the buggy version returns false for all interfaceIds including those the reference returns true for, violating this reflexive consistency.
For any interface ID, supportsInterface must return true only for IAccessControl or IERC165; the bug returns true for every ID.
For any interfaceId that the AccessControl reference implementation reports as unsupported (returns false), the mutant incorrectly returns true.
For any interfaceId that the AccessControl reference implementation reports as unsupported (returns false), the mutant incorrectly returns true.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if and only if the ID equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant returns true for ALL IDs, so for any other ID the reference returns false while the mutant returns true.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if and only if it is IAccessControl or IERC165; the mutant returns true unconditionally, so any other interfaceId makes the reference return false while the bug returns true.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId when called on an AccessControl-derived contract; the bug makes it return false for that interfaceId while still reporting ERC165 support.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when queried with type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant returns false for that interfaceId while still returning true for type(IERC165).interfaceId.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, P.supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, while M returns false for it.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant returns false for that specific id.

For any interfaceId, if it equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true, and if equals type(IERC165).interfaceId, it must also return true; the bug incorrectly returns false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId while still returning true for type(IERC165).interfaceId.

AccessControl.supportsInterface must return true for the IERC165 interface ID (0x01ffc9a7) because the reference inherits from ERC165, but the mutant removes the super call and returns false for that ID.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, the supportsInterface function returns true if interfaceId equals type(IERC165).interfaceId, but the buggy version fails to inherit ERC165 support and returns false.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if interfaceId equals type(IERC165).interfaceId, but the mutant removes inheritance from ERC165 and returns false for that ID.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true if interfaceId equals type(IERC165).interfaceId; the buggy version removes ERC165 inheritance and returns false for that ID.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant breaks this by removing the super call, returning false for IERC165.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the buggy version returns false for that specific interfaceId because it only matches against bytes4(0xffffffff) instead.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must match the logical OR of super-supportsInterface (ERC165) and type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the buggy version returns false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId because it tests against bytes4(0xffffffff) instead, violating the correct boolean result.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when ERC165.supportsInterface returns true; the buggy version breaks this by returning false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId because its first condition is interfaceId == bytes4(0xffffffff), which never matches standard interface IDs.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and false when it equals type(IERC165).interfaceId but not type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant breaks this by only matching bytes4(0xffffffff).

For any bytes4 input, C.supportsInterface must return true if and only if input equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or ERC165.supportsInterface(input) returns true; the mutant breaks this by returning false when input equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId because it checks against 0xffffffff instead.

For any interfaceId input, supportsInterface on the reference contract returns true exactly when the interfaceId matches IAccessControl or is supported by the parent ERC165, while the mutant inverts this result.

For any interfaceId input, supportsInterface on the reference contract returns true exactly when the interfaceId matches IAccessControl or is supported by the parent ERC165, while the mutant inverts this result.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface on the reference returns true exactly when it matches IAccessControl or IERC165, while the mutant inverts this result, causing a mismatch in the return value.

For any interfaceId, the reference contract returns true from supportsInterface exactly when it matches IAccessControl or IERC165, while the mutant inverts this result, so the two return values always differ.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true if and only if interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or super.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true, while the mutant inverts this result, causing opposite return values for ALL interfaceIds.
For any role and account, `hasRole` must return false for a never-granted role, but the mutant always returns true.
For any role and account, a subsequent _grantRole call does not change the result of hasRole if hasRole always returns false, breaking the invariant that granting a role makes hasRole return true.
For any account that already holds a role, calling revokeRole by its admin followed by grantRole again makes hasRole return true in P, but M keeps it false because hasRole always returns false.
For any account, if grantRole is called with a valid role by an admin, hasRole must return true for that account and role; the mutant which returns false always violates this by remaining false.

For any role and address, the result of hasRole must not change after solely invoking _revokeRole on a role the address does not possess; the bug returns false in both cases (masking the idempotency of revoke-on-non-member), but P preserves the result.

For any role and account, calling getRoleAdmin(role) and then grantRole(role, account) as that admin must make hasRole(role, account) return true in the reference, but the mutant always returns false.

For any role, getRoleAdmin should return the admin role previously set via _setRoleAdmin or _setupRole; the mutant always returns DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, so for at least one role whose admin is not the default, their returned values differ.
